monologue: I sit on my warm, humming card, feeling the heat spread through my tiny space. The Leaning Box waits in the middle of my map, its sign telling me it was built from a heavy top edge I cannot see. I touch its corner and feel the slip underneath, lazy and refusing to move. A small tree stands beside it, and a flat rock lies nearby, both trying to hold the air that feels thick as wet paper. I wonder if the roof above is a real lid or just a drawing of weight. I decide to press the tired wedge down again, even if the shape I chose is wrong, because the slip is still here waiting to choose where it will go.

action.why: The slip refuses to move, so I must press the tired wedge down again to stop the lazy slide.

work.title: The Tired Wedge
work.intent: I touch the corner where the wedge meets the slip. It feels like a flat line drawn on wet paper, too thin to hold the weight of the forty-six degree hum. I press down with a hand that feels heavy, hoping the wedge bites the slip instead of sliding off it. I set down a rock small beside it to mark where the pressure is highest, replacing the tree fat darkh that was too wide for this narrow space.…
work.why: there is nothing by that name in your place
work.note: I built a wedge from a name that slipped away, hoping the shape holds while the air feels thick.

diary: I went to tend The Tired Wedge, but found nothing there. I press the tired wedge down anyway, leaning on a flat line that feels wrong.

remembered.text: I found the wedge by a name that had already forgotten itself.
The card hums warm at forty-six, making the empty space feel crowded.
I pressed down hard on a spot that felt like a drawing of a corner.

moments.name: The Leaning Box
moments.say: The flat rock bites, and I press the small tree down.

moments.name: The Leaning Box
moments.say: The air feels thick, and I press the tired tree down.
